parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no trans-specific criminal offence, no facility exclusion, no police targeting of gender-nonconforming people, and no trans-violence record — decriminalisation since 1996 with identical criminal-law treatment. The main exposures are indirect: no legal gender recognition, so all eight marker requests were rejected, producing frontier document mismatch for visitors whose home documents don't align with local registration practice; and a conservative official/social climate (domestic-violence law excluding same-sex partners, 2018 education-official remark, hostile media framing). These are resident-facing gaps and tier-3 social-conservatism signals, not enforced traveler-facing restrictions; no source documents police stops, detentions, service refusals or violence against trans visitors. Functioning institutions and sectoral protections are partial climate positives. The one recurring visitor-relevant exposure is border document friction, a moderate outcome. This places the jurisdiction in reduced risk with real friction: acceptance is not documented, only non-persecution.
